outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: The Challenge of Infinite Context
outline.description: Introduces Large Language Models (LLMs) and the critical importance of context window size. It details why expanding context beyond 128k tokens is notoriously difficult, citing specific barriers such as catastrophic forgetting, data scarcity, computational cost, and attention dispersion.
subtopics: Role of Context Windows in Modern AI Applications
Current Limitations: Why Most LLMs Cap at 4k–128k Tokens
Three Major Obstacles to Extreme Extension: Catastrophic Values, Data Scarcity, and Computational Cost
The Problem of Attention Dispersion and Performance Degradation

outline.description: Provides a technical primer on RoPE, the foundational mechanism used in modern transformers. Explains the mathematical formulation of RoPE, how it encodes relative positions via rotation matrices, and reviews existing strategies for modifying these rotations during context extension (Linear PI, NTK, YaRN).
subtopics: Mathematical Foundations of Rotational Position Embedding (Equations & Intuition)
How Rotation Angles Encode Relative Distance Between Tokens
Review of Baseline Methods: Linear Position Interpolation (PI)
Advanced Heuristics: NTK-Aware Extrapolation and YaRN Grouping Strategies

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Discovering Non-Uniformities in Positional Encoding
outline.description: Details the core theoretical contribution of the paper. Through systematic analysis and empirical testing, it demonstrates that uniform interpolation is suboptimal. It defines two distinct 'non-uniformities': variations across RoPE dimensions and sensitivity to initial token positions.
subtopics: $Evaluating Sub-optimality: Why Current Heuristics Fail at Scale$
$Finding 1$: Dimension-Specific Sensitivity – Low Frequencies Need Less Scaling Than High Ones"
$Finding 2$: Token Position Bias – Initial Tokens Require Minimal Interpolation"$}
